facts.text: Manatee Road is named after the West Indian manatees that frequent the nearby Withlacoochee River, a key habitat for these endangered marine mammals.
The area was originally settled in the late 19th century as a logging and farming community, with the Withlacoochee River serving as a vital transport route for timber and goods.
The region encompassing Manatee Road has been inhabited by indigenous peoples for thousands of years, with archaeological evidence indicating human presence dating back at least 13,000 years.
In the early 19th century, the area fell under Seminole influence, as the Seminole Nation occupied northern Florida lands that would become Levy County after the Seminole Wars.
Situated in Levy County, Manatee Road is known for its proximity to the Gulf of Mexico and the Nature Coast.
Manatee Road enjoys a warm, humid climate typical of Florida, drawing visitors who seek a quiet retreat into nature.
